records.name: ACCT Philly
records.summary: The shelter on Hunting Park Avenue where volunteers walk dogs, socialize cats, and help at adoption events. The group also runs a trap-neuter-return program for outdoor cats.
records.what_you_do: Walk and socialize dogs, socialize cats, clean cages, greet adopters, or help with laundry and the food pantry. Groups and companies can also come in for a shelter day.

schedule.text: Main shelter volunteers give at least 3 hours a month. Group and company visits are arranged by email.

first_step.how: Watch the general orientation on the website, pass its quiz, then fill out the volunteer application. Approval can take up to a week.
first_step.basis: An online orientation, quiz and application come before a first shift, so getting in takes a week or more.

records.notes: Two ACCT pages print different phone numbers ((267) 385-3800 and 215-385-3800 ext. 114), so no phone is listed. The community cats coordinator can be reached at communitycats@acctphilly.org. TNR appointments are booked through the scheduling link on the community cats page. A 2019 WHYY article calls ACCT the city's animal control agency; the pages read here did not say whether ACCT is a nonprofit, so please check the kind field.

records.name: PAWS Philadelphia
records.summary: Philadelphia Animal Welfare Society runs cat and dog care shifts seven days a week at its Old City and Grays Ferry sites. It also places shelter animals in volunteer foster homes.
records.what_you_do: Socialize and feed cats, walk and play with dogs, help at adoption events, or do office and upkeep work. You can also foster a shelter animal at home for a few weeks.

schedule.text: Cat care and cleaning shifts run seven days a week at the Old City and Grays Ferry sites.

first_step.how: Complete the online volunteer application on the volunteer page, or email or call the site you want to help at.
first_step.basis: An online application comes first, and the page does not say how long approval takes.

records.notes: The newest dated item is the Mutt Strut 2026 sponsor list, so the status is active, but no month is printed and last_sign_of_life is left out. The Northeast Spay/Neuter and Wellness Clinic at 1810 Grant Avenue was not listed because its volunteer program is on hold. Minimum age and cost are not stated on the pages read. Fostering contact is foster@phillypaws.org, shown on the get-involved page.

records.name: Pennsylvania SPCA
records.summary: The Pennsylvania SPCA's Philadelphia headquarters on East Erie Avenue offers hands-on volunteer work with dogs, cats and adoption events, plus a foster program.
records.what_you_do: Walk dogs, socialize cats and kittens, help at off-site adoption events, plan fundraisers, do office work, or foster an animal at home.

first_step.how: Choose the program you want on the volunteer page, then use its Apply link for the Philadelphia location.
first_step.basis: Each location has its own application, and volunteers are trained before they work with little supervision.

records.notes: The volunteer pages print no dates, so status rests on a working site with no dated items. Schedule, commitment and cost are not stated. The phone is the main line from the contact page. The Philadelphia location page links to a volunteer section for campus work; team volunteering for companies is also offered.

records.name: Morris Animal Refuge
records.summary: A shelter on Lombard Street that takes volunteers for animal care, dog walks and cat socialization. Its South Philadelphia PetSmart adoption center also needs cat care volunteers.
records.what_you_do: Care for animals, walk dogs, socialize cats, move animals between sites, take photos and write animal bios, or help at fundraising events.

schedule.text: Shelter time slots depend on the role. PetSmart cat care shifts last 3 hours.

first_step.how: Fill out the Shelter Volunteering Interest Form. Ages 14 to 17 use a separate under 18 form. PetSmart volunteers use their own interest form.
first_step.basis: An interest form comes first, and the main shelter program had a waitlist as of January 2025.

records.notes: The newest dated item is a waitlist note that says January 2025. The PetSmart role is still taking applications, with no date given. Corporate, academic and other groups can book a volunteer day through the volunteer group page. Cost is not listed.

records.name: Schuylkill Center Wildlife Clinic
records.summary: The wildlife clinic of the Schuylkill Center cares for sick, injured and orphaned native wildlife so healthy animals can go back to the wild. Volunteers do clinic support, and adults can join animal care work.
records.what_you_do: Clinic support means cleaning, laundry, dishes, enclosure setup and diet prep. Animal care adds weighing patients, recording food intake, and hand feeding orphaned birds and mammals.

schedule.text: At least one 4-hour shift a week, about 20 hours a month. Animal care volunteers must keep a strict shift schedule.

first_step.how: Complete the online volunteer application, attend a volunteer training session, and sign the volunteer agreement. The application also sends notice of future training sessions.
first_step.basis: Application, training and a weekly shift come first, though animal care needs no veterinary or animal handling background.

records.notes: In-person training sessions were listed for February 7 and February 28, 2026. The clinic does not allow public tours. Injured wildlife goes through the clinic hotline (215-482-7300, option 2), not the volunteer route. Drop-off hours are on the clinic page.

records.name: Audubon Mid-Atlantic
records.summary: The regional Audubon group leads public bird walks in Philadelphia parks, including several tours for Philly Birding Weekend in October.
records.what_you_do: Join a guided bird walk in a city park, or take a kayak or bike birding trip on the river.

schedule.text: Philly Birding Weekend tours on October 10 and 11, most starting at 8 am.

locations.label: Discovery Center and East Fairmount Park

cost.text: Not printed on the listing page

first_step.how: Choose a walk on the listing and follow its event link to sign up.
first_step.basis: Walks are open to the public with an event link for each one, but the listing does not say whether sign up is required.

records.notes: The listings print month and day only, with no year in the visible text, so no year is recorded here. The page names no Philadelphia chapter, so this record covers the regional group's Philadelphia walks only. The Morris Arboretum listing links to a sign up page that was not read. The Delaware Valley Ornithological Club could not be read (HTTP 403).

records.name: Comfort Caring Canines
records.summary: A Collegeville nonprofit that brings certified therapy dog teams to nursing homes, hospitals and reading programs across southeastern Pennsylvania. It also runs a crisis support team for school districts.
records.what_you_do: A handler and dog visit residents, patients or children in reading programs. Handlers choose when to visit, and each new facility must approve the visit first.

schedule.text: Each volunteer team chooses when to visit. Certification evaluation dates are posted on the group's events calendar.

locations.label: Collegeville office (mailing address is a P.O. Box)

first_step.how: Check the dog requirements, watch the orientation video, then email to register for a certification evaluation.
first_step.basis: A dog must pass a temperament and obedience exam, and handlers need background checks before they can visit.

records.notes: The site lists no dated events or news, so status rests on a working site. The crisis support team serves school districts. Cost to join is not stated. A search snippet (not read) says the Philadelphia Family Court uses this group's dog teams, so that claim is unverified here. The general contact email is info@comfortcaringcanines.com.

records.name: Wagging Tails Brigade
records.summary: A volunteer program at Philadelphia International Airport where certified therapy dog teams spend about two hours a week in the terminals, helping travelers and staff relax.
records.what_you_do: A handler and dog walk the terminals and visit with passengers, who can take home a trading card with the dog's picture. Handlers fill out an interest form to join.

schedule.text: About two hours a week in the airport terminals.

first_step.how: Fill out the interest form linked on the program page. The page does not say what happens after that.
first_step.basis: The way in is an interest form, and certification and age rules are not stated on the page.

records.notes: The airport runs this program itself, and the airport is a city department, so decide whether it fits the government office rule. The program page is current but undated; the newest dated item is a July 22, 2022 news post welcoming three dog teams. The program page says it works with the Alliance of Therapy Dogs, which was not read. Age minimum and cost are not stated.

records.name: CHOP Pet Therapy Program
records.summary: The Gerald B. Shreiber Pet Therapy Program at Children's Hospital of Philadelphia sends dog and handler teams room to room to visit patients, giving them a break from their hospital room.
records.what_you_do: A handler and screened therapy dog visit patients during a monthly shift, after a two-hour unit and patient care orientation. The program coordinator goes along on the first three visits.

schedule.text: At least one two-hour shift a month at the Philadelphia hospital. The King of Prussia spots are full.

first_step.how: Request an interview through the program's contact page. After that come health clearance, background checks and orientation.
first_step.basis: A handler and dog need an interview, a health screening, background checks and a current registration with a therapy dog group.

records.notes: The program page is current but undated. The only dated item found is a September 25, 2019 article. CHOP Volunteer Services pays for health clearances and background checks. The phone is the Child Life, Education and Creative Arts Therapy department line from the article. Other costs, such as the owner's own vet visits, are not covered according to the page.

records.name: Project MEOW
records.summary: An all volunteer West Philadelphia cat group that helps homeless cats through trap, neuter, return and manage work, feeds colony cats, and finds homes for friendly abandoned cats.
records.what_you_do: Feed colony cats once a week, foster or transport cats, help at tabling and fundraising events, or join the design, social media or grant teams.

schedule.text: Colony feeding is once a week, from 4 to 7 pm, for about an hour, and needs a vehicle. Other roles have flexible hours.

locations.label: Colony sites within 2 miles of Clark Park

first_step.how: Complete the volunteer application on the group's website, or email rfa@projectmeow.org.
first_step.basis: An application comes first, and some roles need a vehicle or lifting about 20 pounds.

records.notes: The home page has a 'Cats Helped in 2026' section, which is a year total and not a dated item, so status is probably active rather than active. The footer year 2025 is not used. The group's pages print no ZIP codes or neighborhoods. Pages on fostering and the volunteer application were linked but not read.

records.name: Stray Cat Relief Fund
records.summary: A South Philadelphia nonprofit that traps, neuters, vaccinates and returns stray cats, lends humane traps to residents, and rescues and adopts out cats from its adoption center.
records.what_you_do: Trap and transport cats, help with colony care, or foster cats through the group's foster program.

first_step.how: Email purr@straycatrelieffund.org, or use the volunteer, fostering or foster application pages linked from the site.
first_step.basis: Separate applications exist for volunteering and fostering, and the page does not describe the steps after applying.

records.notes: The newest dated item is a 2024 total (138 cats in TNVR services, 320 rescued cats adopted). The footer year 2023 is not used. Volunteer age and cost are not stated, and the linked volunteer and foster pages were not read. Events are named but have no dates. The P.O. Box is the only address printed.

leads_only.note: Named in an older AKC article describing therapy dog teams that visit medical sites, schools and nursing homes. The club's own site was not found, and the article date was not confirmed.
